(xviii) Required Transmission Enhancements Designed to Address Stability Issues.
For purposes of the assignment of cost responsibility for Reliability Projects designed to address 
stability issues under subsection (b)(i)(A)(2)(a) and subsection (b)(ii)(A) of this Schedule 12, the 
Transmission Provider shall, using the same inputs and assumptions from the simulation that 
originally drove the need for the stability upgrade, perform a stability simulation that includes 
the stability upgrade under the worst fault condition. The worst fault condition shall be the fault 
condition in the simulation that produces the maximum rotor angle swing with the stability 
upgrade included.  For each load bus on the system, the difference between the highest and 
lowest voltage angle that occurs during the simulation of the worst fault condition will be 
recorded. Load buses having a voltage angle deviation less than 25 percent of the load bus with 
the largest voltage angle deviation will not be included in the cost allocation calculation. For the 
remaining load buses, the voltage angle deviation will be multiplied by the megawatt load at the 
bus obtained from the stability simulation model, or, in the case of a Merchant Transmission 
Facility, the Firm Transmission Withdrawal Rights at the bus. The products of the voltage angle 
deviation and megawatt load at each bus will be summed for each Responsible Zone. The 
Page 103

Stability Deviation cost allocation for a Responsible Zone or Merchant Transmission Facility 
will be determined by dividing the sum of the load-weighted angle deviations for the 
Responsible Zone or Merchant Transmission Facility by the sum of the load-weighted angle 
deviations for each Responsible Zone and Merchant Transmission Facility. Transmission 
Provider shall round cost responsibility assignments to the nearest one-hundredth of one percent.

SCHEDULE 22
Financial Penalty Charge for 
Unreserved Use by Eligible Load and Large Load
An Eligible Customer taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service, or Interim Network Integration Transmission Service on behalf 
of Eligible Load or Large Load shall be subject to financial penalties for its unreserved use of the 
transmission system.
The financial penalty charge for unreserved use shall include two components: (1) a base penalty 
charge, which applies to each individual hour in which the reserved transmission service limit is 
exceeded, and (2) a penalty ratchet, which applies when such exceedances occur repeatedly.
Base Penalty Charge
When an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Eligible Load or Large Load exceeds its 
reserved transmission service limit, a base penalty charge shall be assessed for any hour in which 
at least one five-minute interval occurs during which the Eligible Customer’s telemetered load at 
the Point of Delivery exceeds its reserved transmission service limit.  This five-minute interval is 
defined as an Exceedance Interval, and such an hour is defined as an Exceedance Hour.  The 
base penalty charge shall apply to each Exceedance Hour.  
For an Eligible Customer taking only Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, the 
reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service minus any curtailed MW.  
For an Eligible Customer taking only Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, 
the reserved transmission service limit shall equal the approved Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service minus any curtailed MW.  
For an Eligible Customer taking Firm Contract Demand and Non-Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Services, the reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service plus the approved Non-Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service minus any curtailed MW.  
For an Eligible Customer taking Interim Network Integration Transmission Service, the 
reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Interim Network Integration 
Transmission Service demand minus any curtailed MW.
Each five-minute interval beginning with the first minute of each hour shall constitute a 
separate interval and each hour from 0100 through 2400 shall constitute a separate hour 
for purposes of determining whether one or more exceedances have occurred.
Page 115

The base penalty charge shall be applied to each Exceedance Hour and shall be calculated as:
Hourly Exceedance MW × Equivalent Hourly Firm Contract Demand (“FCD”) rate × 
number of Exceedance Intervals within the hour
Where:
Hourly Exceedance MW = Maximum telemetered load during the hour – Reserved 
Transmission Service Limit for the hour
Equivalent Hourly FCD rate = FCD rate / 8,760 hours
Penalty Ratchet
A penalty rachet shall apply when multiple Exceedance Hours occur during a particular time 
period in order to escalate the penalty charges as the frequency of unreserved transmission use 
increases.  
If more than one Exceedance Hour occurs on the same calendar day, an additional daily 
penalty shall apply.  
If exceedances occur on multiple calendar days within the same calendar week, an 
additional weekly penalty shall apply. 
If exceedances occur in multiple calendar weeks within the same calendar month, an 
additional monthly penalty shall apply.
If exceedances occur in multiple calendar months within the same calendar year, an 
additional yearly penalty shall apply.  
The penalty ratchet shall be based on an Eligible Customer’s exceedance pattern and applies 
escalating FCD-equivalent rates as the frequency of unreserved transmission use increases.  
Depending on whether exceedances occur within the same calendar day, calendar week, calendar 
month, or calendar year, the penalty ratchet shall apply daily, weekly, monthly, or annual penalty 
charges, respectively, as follows:

Weekly FCD-Equivalent Rate

The Daily Penalty Charge is calculated as:

× Daily FCD Equivalent Rate

× Number of Exceedance Hours in the calendar day

The Weekly Penalty Charge is calculated as:
Maximum Hourly Exceedance MW during the calendar week
× Weekly FCD Equivalent Rate

The Monthly Penalty Charge is calculated as:

Sub-Annual Resource Reliability Target: 
“Sub-Annual Reliability Target” for the PJM Region or an LDA, shall mean the maximum 
amount of the combination of Extended Summer Demand Resources and Limited Demand 
Resources in Unforced Capacity determined by PJM to be consistent with the maintenance of 
reliability, stated in Unforced Capacity, that shall be used to calculate the Minimum Annual 
Resource Requirement for Delivery Years through May 31, 2017 and the Sub-Annual Resource 
Constraint for the 2017/2018 and 2018/2019 Delivery Years.  As more fully set forth in the PJM 
Manuals, PJM calculates the Sub-Annual Resource Reliability Target, by first determining a 
reference annual loss of load expectation (“LOLE”) assuming no Demand Resources.  The 
calculation for the unconstrained portion of the PJM Region uses a daily distribution of loads 
under a range of weather scenarios (based on the most recent load forecast and iteratively 
shifting the load distributions to result in the Installed Reserve Margin established for the 
Delivery Year in question) and a weekly capacity distribution (based on the cumulative capacity 
availability distributions developed for the Installed Reserve Margin study for the Delivery Year 
in question).  The calculation for each relevant LDA uses a daily distribution of loads under a 
range of weather scenarios (based on the most recent load forecast for the Delivery Year in 
question) and a weekly capacity distribution (based on the cumulative capacity availability 
distributions developed for the Capacity Emergency Transfer Objective study for the Delivery 
Year in question).  For the relevant LDA calculation, the weekly capacity distributions are 
adjusted to reflect the Capacity Emergency Transfer Limit for the Delivery Year in question.
For both the PJM Region and LDA analyses, PJM then models the commitment of varying 
amounts of DR (displacing otherwise committed generation) as interruptible from May 1 through 
October 31 and unavailable from November 1 through April 30 and calculates the LOLE at each 
DR level.  The Extended Summer DR Reliability Target is the DR amount, stated as a percentage 
of the unrestricted peak load, that produces no more than a ten percent increase in the LOLE, 
compared to the reference value.  The Sub-Annual Resource Reliability Target shall be 
expressed as a percentage of the forecasted peak load of the PJM Region or such LDA and is

converted to Unforced Capacity by multiplying [the reliability target percentage] times [the 
Forecast Pool Requirement] times [the DR Factor] times [the forecasted peak load of the PJM 
Region or such LDA, reduced by the amount of load served under the FRR Alternative].

Tariff, Part VIII, Subpart N, section 441
Cost Recovery Protection for Firm Transmission Service
(a) Cost Recovery Assurances: With respect to Eligible Customers that intend to request any 
form of Firm Transmission Service from Transmission Provider on behalf of an Eligible Load or 
Large Load, a Transmission Owner shall either:
(i)
Enter into a Cost Recovery Agreement in the form found in Tariff, Part IX, 
Subpart P with the applicable Eligible Customer and Eligible Load or Large Load.  The 
Transmission Owner counterparty shall be the Transmission Owner that owns the transmission 
facilities with which the Eligible Load or Large Load will interconnect.  In the case of an 
Eligible Load or Large Load that will not directly interconnect with a Transmission Owner, the 
Transmission Owner counterparty shall be the Transmission Owner to which the applicable 
Eligible Customer is connected and from whom the Eligible Customer intends to take Firm 
Transmission Service.  The purpose of the Cost Recovery Agreement is to ensure the Eligible 
Customer takes a minimum level of Firm Transmission Service on behalf of the Eligible Load or 
Large Load based on the committed load level and the applicable rate for the Firm Transmission 
Service, or, if not, the Eligible Load or Large Load shall be required to make a shortfall payment 
representing any difference between the committed minimum level of service and the actual 
level of service taken.
(ii)
Enter into, subject to FERC acceptance, a separate agreement between at least the 
Transmission Owner and an Eligible Load or Large Load to prevent cost shifting among 
transmission customers.  Such separate agreement will be determined to adequately prevent cost 
shifts if such agreement, in conjunction with relevant federal and state regulatory requirements, 
including applicable retail service tariffs, results in minimum Firm Transmission Service and 
credit standards, or other comparable protections.
An Eligible Customer and/or Eligible Load or Large Load will be required to enter into and 
execute a Cost Recovery Agreement or an agreement that meets the standards set forth in 
subsection (a)(ii) in order to proceed past the Soft Close Date associated with the applicable PJM 
Fast Energization Cycle, and obtain any form of Firm Transmission Service from the 
Transmission Provider.
(b) Preservation of Legacy Treatment: No Cost Recovery Agreement or separate agreement 
under subsection (a) above shall be required with respect to Eligible Load or Large Loads 
covered by existing agreements that meet the criteria set forth in subsection (a)(ii) that have 
already been filed and are pending acceptance, or that have been accepted by FERC.  Any 
agreement entered into prior to the effective date of this subsection not filed with FERC will not 
be required to be filed and accepted by FERC; provided, however, in any complaint filed 
pursuant to Section 206 of the Federal Power Act in which it is claimed that such agreement is 
not just and reasonable or is unduly discriminatory within the meaning of the Federal Power Act, 
such agreement shall not be determined to be unjust and unreasonable or unduly discriminatory 
if it meets the standard set forth in subsection (a)(ii).
(c) Tender and Negotiation of Cost Recovery Agreement:  As applicable, consistent with 
subsections (a) and (b) above, Transmission Owner shall tender a draft of the Cost Recovery 
Page 21

Agreement to Eligible Customer and Eligible Load or Large Load within 30 days of the 
completion of the Transmission Owner’s retail load interconnection study.  
Upon receipt of the draft Cost Recovery Agreement, Eligible Customer, as well as the Eligible 
Load or Large Load, shall provide the Transmission Owner with any written comments on the 
draft Cost Recovery Agreement within seven (7) days. The parties will conduct further 
negotiations as required, with such negotiations to be completed within twenty-five (25) days of 
the Transmission Owner’s tender of the draft Cost Recovery Agreement.  
(d) Execution and Filing of Cost Recovery Agreement: Not later than ten (10) days after the 
end of the negotiation period set forth in subsection (c) above, Eligible Customer and the Eligible 
Load or Large Load shall (i) execute the Cost Recovery Agreement and return it to Transmission 
Owner; and (ii) provide the Credit Support specified in the Cost Recovery Agreement.
If the Eligible Load or Large Load fails to execute the Cost Recovery Agreement or provide the 
required Credit Support in the specified time period, Eligible Customer shall not be permitted to 
proceed through the applicable Fast Energization Cycle.  
The Transmission Owner shall file any executed Cost Recovery Agreement, if required, with 
FERC within twenty-one (21) days of the other parties executing the Cost Recovery Agreement.
(e) Crediting of Termination Amounts: If the effective date of an Early Termination or Partial 
Termination, as defined in a Cost Recovery Agreement, occurs prior to the first Service Date 
specified in such agreement, and the Eligible Load or Large Load that is a party to that 
agreement is required to make a termination payment, as applicable, such termination payment 
or other amounts received pursuant to such obligation, including any security drawn on by 
Transmission Owner, shall be divided amongst the pool of Transmission Owners constructing
facilities needed to provide the related transmission service, but which will no longer be 
constructed, including the Transmission Owner that is a party to the Cost Recovery Agreement, 
as follows:
(i)
Within thirty (30) days of such termination, the Transmission Owner that is party 
to the Cost Recovery Agreement (referred to herein as the “contracting Transmission Owner”) 
shall notify all other Transmission Owners that have been designated to construct and own 
Interconnection Reliability Reinforcements necessary to provide Firm Transmission Service to 
an Eligible Customer on behalf of the terminating Eligible Load or Large Load (referred to 
herein as the “third party Transmission Owners”) of such termination.  For purposes of this 
subsection, third party Transmission Owners shall include all Transmission Owners designated 
to construct and own Interconnection Reliability Reinforcements identified in the PJM Fast 
Energization Cycle in which the terminating Eligible Load or Large Load was studied, and for 
which the contracting Transmission Owner’s Zone received a cost responsibility share.
(ii)
Each third-party Transmission Owner shall, within thirty (30) days of the deadline 
for filings its FERC Form 1 that includes all Eligible Costs, provide an account of such Eligible 
Costs to the contracting Transmission Owner.  For purposes of this subsection “Eligible Costs” 
consist of all expenditures, costs, and cancellation fees incurred or due to commitments made by 
the third-party Transmission Owner to engineer, design, procure, construct, own, operate,

maintain, and service the Interconnection Reliability Reinforcements needed to serve the Eligible 
Customer taking transmission service on behalf of the Eligible Load or Large Load, but which 
will no longer be constructed, which (a) are incurred through the end of the calendar year in 
which notice of termination was received from the contracting Transmission Owner, and (b) are 
included in amounts reported in the Transmission Owner’s FERC Form 1 covering that calendar 
year.  
Any failure by a third-party Transmission Owner to provide such information within the 
timeframe above shall bar said Transmission Owner from receiving a portion of amounts paid by 
Eligible Load or Large Load as set forth below.
(iii)
Within thirty (30) days of (a) receiving all Transmission Owner accountings in 
accordance with subsection (ii) above, and (b) receipt of termination amounts from the Eligible 
Load or Large Load that is party to the Cost Recovery Agreement,  the contracting Transmission 
Owner shall divide such termination amounts among itself and the pool of third-party 
Transmission Owners based on each Transmission Owner’s pro rata share of the total amount of 
applicable expenditures, costs and cancellation fees, and disburse such amounts to the third-party 
Transmission Owners accordingly.  
For purposes of determining these pro rata shares, the contracting Transmission Owner shall be 
permitted to include Eligible Costs associated not only with its applicable Interconnection 
Reliability Reinforcements but also any other transmission facilities, including Supplemental 
Projects and Direct Connection Facilities, that it was constructing in order to provide 
interconnection or transmission service to the Eligible Load or Large Load, or Eligible Customer 
taking transmission service on behalf of the Eligible Load or Large Load.
To the extent that additional termination funds are received or collected from the Eligible Load 
or Large Load after an initial distribution is made under this subsection, contracting 
Transmission Owner will make additional disbursements using the same methodology within 
fifteen (15) days of receipt of such amounts.
(iv)
Nothing in this subsection (e) is intended or shall be interpreted to prevent any 
Transmission Owner from seeking cost recovery through an abandoned plant recovery filing 
made with FERC or through any other proceeding, except insofar as the Transmission Owner has 
received amounts pursuant to the process set forth in this subsection (e), it shall be prohibited 
from requesting recovery of such amounts in any future proceeding.
(v)
To the extent a Transmission Owner elects to satisfy its obligation under 
subsection (a) above through a separate agreement as described in subsection (a)(ii), it shall 
include in such separate agreement reasonably comparable termination payment crediting

(vi)
Any disputes under this subsection (e) shall be subject to the dispute resolution 
procedure set forth in Schedule 5 of the Operating Agreement.

ARTICLE 3
FIRM LOAD COMMITMENT
3.1
Initial Load Commitment and Firm Load Commitment
At execution of this CRA, the Initial Load Commitment shall be established using the amount 
and type of Firm Transmission Service that Eligible Customer intends to request from PJM on 
behalf of Large Load Customer through the applicable application and study process, together 
with the proposed load ramp and anticipated Service Dates identified in Exhibit A.
Following execution of the Final PJM Agreement, the Firm Load Commitment applicable during 
each Measurement Period shall be the amount and type of Firm Transmission Service that the 
Eligible Customer takes on behalf of the Large Load during each Measurement Period, as set 
forth in Exhibit A.  This amount shall be based on the amount of load for the Large Load 
scheduled to be in service during each Measurement Period, or the amount of Firm Transmission 
Service that the Eligible Customer has contracted for on behalf of the Large Load.
Page 30

If Exhibit A establishes a load ramp, consistent with the amount of Firm Transmission Service 
that the Eligible Customer has contracted for on behalf of the Large Load, each scheduled load 
level becomes part of the Firm Load Commitment on the applicable Service Date.
Except as expressly provided in this CRA, Eligible Customer’s failure to begin taking Firm 
Transmission Service to serve the Large Load Facilities, take Firm Transmission Service
corresponding to a scheduled load level, or maintain that level of Firm Transmission Service
does not reduce or defer the Firm Load Commitment or the Committed Revenue Contribution, or 
excuse Large Load Customer from any payment or Credit Support obligation under this CRA.
3.2
Post-Final PJM Agreement Update and Subsequent Modification
Within thirty (30) days after execution of the Final PJM Agreement, Transmission Owner shall 
update Exhibit A to reflect the Firm Transmission Service, load ramp, and Service Dates 
established through or consistent with the Final PJM Agreement. Transmission Owner shall also 
update the Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate, Projected Committed Revenue 
Contributions, Projected Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmarks, Credit Support 
Requirement, the applicable schedules in Exhibits A and C, and the calculations under Exhibit B 
using the information then available.
The information reflected in the Final PJM Agreement shall control over the corresponding 
preliminary information included in Exhibit A at execution. If the Final PJM Agreement 
establishes less Firm Transmission Service than the Initial Load Commitment, the Firm Load 
Commitment shall be reduced accordingly. A reduction required by this paragraph shall not 
constitute a Partial Termination and shall not result in a Partial Termination Amount.
An update required by this Section shall become effective without further agreement of the 
Parties and shall not constitute an amendment to this CRA. Transmission Owner shall provide 
the updated Exhibits and reasonable supporting calculations to Eligible Customer and Large 
Load Customer.
After the update required by this Section, a further modification to the Firm Load Commitment 
or a Service Date shall become effective only if the Parties execute any amendment required 
under this CRA and the amendment receives any required PJM or FERC acceptance or approval. 
A customer-requested reduction remains subject to Article 9.
3.3
No Transmission Owner Obligation
Except as otherwise explicitly provided herein, nothing in this Agreement shall constitute an 
obligation on the part of Transmission Owner to provide any service to any Party or place into 
service any transmission facilities by any specific date or dates.

ARTICLE 5
REVENUE CONTRIBUTIONS AND SHORTFALL AMOUNT
5.1
Committed Revenue Contribution
For each Measurement Period during the Term, Transmission Owner  shall calculate the 
Committed Revenue Contribution in accordance with this Section and Exhibit B, using the 
applicable rates, billing determinants, and other information available in accordance with the 
PJM Tariff.  The Committed Revenue Contribution shall equal the Minimum Commitment 
Percentage multiplied by the Firm Transmission Service-related charges that would apply if 
Eligible Customer took Firm Transmission Service corresponding to the Firm Load Commitment 
applicable during the Measurement Period.
The calculation shall use:
(a) the Firm Load Commitment that applies during each Measurement Period;
(b) the Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate and the generally applicable billing 
determinants under the PJM Tariff; and
(c) the portion of the Measurement Period during which each scheduled Firm Load 
Commitment amount and Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate applies.
If more than one Firm Load Commitment amount or Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate 
applies during a Measurement Period, Transmission Owner 
shall calculate separately the 
amount applicable to each portion of the Measurement Period and aggregate those amounts to 
determine the Committed Revenue Contribution for the applicable Measurement Period.
Eligible Customer shall be responsible for timely payment of charges for Firm Transmission 
Service in a given calendar year on a monthly basis in accordance with the PJM Tariff.
5.2
Actual Revenue Contribution
For each Measurement Period during the Term, Transmission Owner shall calculate the Actual 
Revenue Contribution attributable to Firm Transmission Service actually taken to serve the 
Large Load Facilities in accordance with Exhibit B.  To the extent that the Large Load Customer 
has made separate payments through a retail tariff or other retail mechanism that reflect the 
assignment of Firm Transmission Service or related costs to the Large Load Customer, such 
Page 32

payments shall be taken into account in determining its Actual Revenue Contribution, insofar as 
doing so does not result in costs being shifted to other Eligible Customers taking service in the 
Transmission Owner’s Zone. To the extent that the applicable Firm Transmission Service 
methodology calculates charges using an assigned Network Service Peak Load contribution or 
another allocated billing determinant, the Actual Revenue Contribution shall be calculated using 
the billing determinant assigned to the Large Load Facilities for the applicable Measurement 
Period and the same categories of rates used to calculate the Committed Revenue Contribution.
5.3
Shortfall Amount
For each Measurement Period, the Shortfall Amount shall equal the amount, if any, by which the 
Committed Revenue Contribution exceeds the Actual Revenue Contribution in accordance with 
Exhibit B.
Large Load Customer shall pay each Shortfall Amount in accordance with Article 7.
5.4
Separate Measurement Periods
Each Measurement Period shall be calculated independently.
5.5
Commencement of Committed Revenue Contribution
The determination of the Committed Revenue Contribution and any corresponding Shortfall 
Amounts shall begin on the corresponding Service Date, as set forth in Exhibit A, regardless of 
whether: (i) Eligible Customer has begun taking the corresponding level of Firm Transmission 
Service; (ii) the amount of Firm Transmission Service taken by Eligible Customer corresponds to 
the load level scheduled to apply on that Service Date; or (iii) the Large Load Facilities are 
operating at a lower load level than the one scheduled to apply on that Service Date.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, if Eligible Customer cannot begin taking the applicable Firm 
Transmission Service on a Service Date solely because the necessary transmission facilities have 
not been  completed, and such delay was not  caused in whole or in part by Large Load 
Customer’s or Eligible Customer’s failure or lack of reasonable diligence in satisfying  its 
obligations under this CRA or under any other binding agreement, tariff, regulatory order, or 
other legal requirement, the Service Date and commencement of the corresponding Committed 
Revenue Contribution shall be extended on a day-for-day basis until the Firm Transmission 
Service becomes available.  Large Load Customer’s obligations include, without limitation (a) 
construction, testing, commissioning and readiness of any facilities being constructed by Large 
Load Customer, and (b) prompt and reasonable responses to Transmission Owner’s or 
Transmission Owners’ affiliate(s)’ requests for information, approvals, or other communications 
necessary for Transmission Owner’s or Transmission Owners’ affiliate(s)’ work.
5.6  
Access to Information
Eligible Customer shall provide, or authorize access to, the service, billing, settlement, and 
allocation information from PJM or any other entity reasonably necessary for Transmission 
Owner to calculate the Actual Revenue Contribution, Shortfall Amount, or any other calculation

required under this Agreement.

(c) Transmission Owner has no remaining right to draw on the Credit Support under this 
CRA.

attachments to Exhibit C.

Replacement of Credit Support

ARTICLE 12
FORCE MAJEURE
12.1
Definition and Scope of Force Majeure
“Force Majeure” means an event or circumstance that:
(a) physically and directly impacts the Large Load Facilities, new transmission facilities, 
or modifications to existing transmission facilities, and/or 
(b) prevents the Affected Party from performing its obligations under this CRA, 
which event or circumstance (i) could not have been  reasonably anticipated as of the Effective 
Date and (ii) which is not within the reasonable control of, or the result of negligence or 
misconduct by, the Affected Party, and (iii) which the Affected Party is unable to overcome or 
avoid or cause to be avoided, by the exercise of reasonable care.  Subject to meeting the 
requirements of the prior sentence, Force Majeure events shall include, but not be limited to, acts 
of God; fire; flood; earthquake; war; explosions; labor disputes; lightning; hurricanes; tornadoes; 
pandemics or epidemics; riots; or acts of terrorism that affect one or more Parties.  With respect 
to a Party’s obligation to make payments hereunder, Force Majeure will be only an event or act 
that on any day disables the banking system through which a Party makes such payments.  
Nothing herein shall be construed so as to require a Party to settle any strike or labor dispute in 
which it may be involved.  Economic hardship of any Party shall not constitute a Force Majeure 
under this CRA, even if that economic hardship is caused by an event or condition that would 
have been a Force Majeure event if it has physically and directly impacted the Large Load 
Facilities, new transmission facilities, or modifications to existing transmission facilities.
No event affecting only the Large Load Customer, the Large Load Facilities, or the amount of 
Firm Transmission Service taken to serve the Large Load Facilities shall constitute Force 
Majeure with respect to Large Load Customer’s payment or Credit Support obligations under 
this CRA.
The Party claiming Force Majeure bears the burden of establishing that the event satisfies every 
requirement of this Section.
If a Party is rendered unable, wholly or in part, by Force Majeure to carry out its obligations with 
respect to this CRA (the “Affected Party”), then the obligations of the Affected Party will, to the 
extent they are affected by such Force Majeure event, be suspended during the period of time 
that the Force Majeure event renders the Affected Party unable, wholly or in part, to carry out its 
obligations.  The Affected Party will not be liable for breach of this CRA due to a Force Majeure 
event nor shall the Affected Party be liable to the other Parties for, or on account of, any loss, 
damage, injury, or expense resulting from, or arising out of such Force Majeure event.  The 
Affected Party must give written notice and full particulars of such Force Majeure event as soon 
Page 46

as practical after the occurrence of the Force Majeure event.  If a Force Majeure event continues 
for over 180 days in the aggregate during any 12 month period, the Parties will meet and in good 
faith attempt to renegotiate the terms and conditions of this CRA to address and account for the 
Force Majeure event.  If the Parties are thereafter unable to mutually agree in writing on an 
amendment to this CRA to address issues arising out of the Force Majeure event, Transmission 
Owner or Large Load Customer may terminate this CRA upon ten (10) days’ written notice to 
the other Parties, subject to Section 12.2, Article 9, and any obligations that accrued or survive 
under this CRA.
12.2
Termination Due to Force Majeure   
In the event that Large Load Customer terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 12, the 
Large Load Customer shall remain obligated to pay the Early Termination Amount.  However, if 
the Transmission Owner terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 12, Large Load 
Customer shall not be required to pay the Early Termination Amount.
12.3
Effect of Force Majeure
If a Party is prevented by Force Majeure from performing an obligation under this CRA, that 
obligation shall be suspended only:  (i) to the extent performance is physically impossible 
because of the Force Majeure; (ii) for the period during which performance remains physically 
impossible; and (iii) while the affected Party complies with Section 12.4.
The affected Party shall not be in breach of this CRA solely because it fails to perform an 
obligation properly suspended under this Section.
Force Majeure does not:
(a) excuse or delay an obligation to pay an amount due under this CRA, except solely to 
the extent expressly provided in Section 12.1;
(b) excuse or delay Large Load Customer’s obligation to cause Credit Support to be 
provided, maintained, increased, renewed, replaced, or replenished;
(c) except for an extension of a Service Date expressly permitted under Section 5.5, 
reduce, defer, or otherwise modify the Firm Load Commitment, any Service Date, or the 
Minimum Commitment Percentage;
(d) reduce or defer the calculation of the Committed Revenue Contribution, Actual 
Revenue Contribution, Shortfall Amount, Early Termination Amount, or Partial 
Termination Amount;
(e) excuse Eligible Customer’s failure to take Firm Transmission Service corresponding 
to the Firm Load Commitment;
(f) require Transmission Owner to release or reduce Credit Support;
(g) prevent Transmission Owner from issuing an invoice, completing a calculation or 
reconciliation, or drawing on Credit Support in accordance with this CRA; 
(h) excuse any obligation that arose before the Force Majeure began; or
(i) affect the application of Article 9 to any abandonment, permanent cessation, 
permanent reduction, or termination associated with the Force Majeure.
For the avoidance of doubt, a Force Majeure affecting the Large Load Customer, the Large Load 
Page 47

Facilities, or the amount of Firm Transmission Service taken to serve the Large Load Facilities 
shall not reduce, defer, or otherwise modify Large Load Customer’s payment or Credit Support 
obligations under this CRA. If circumstances associated with a Force Majeure result in 
abandonment, permanent cessation, permanent reduction, or termination, Article 9 shall govern 
the availability, effectiveness, and financial consequences of that abandonment, cessation, 
reduction, or termination.
12.4
Notice
A Party claiming Force Majeure shall provide the other Parties with written notice as soon as 
reasonably practicable after becoming aware of the event.
Failure to provide timely notice shall not prevent an event from qualifying as Force Majeure, but 
the affected Party shall not be excused from performance to the extent the delay in notice 
materially prejudices  another Party.

EXHIBIT B
REVENUE CONTRIBUTION AND SHORTFALL CALCULATION
1. Applicable Firm Load Commitment
For each Measurement Period, the “Applicable Firm Load Commitment” shall mean each 
amount of the Firm Load Commitment scheduled to apply during that Measurement Period 
under Exhibit A.
If more than one load level is scheduled to apply during a Measurement Period, each load level 
shall apply for the portion of the Measurement Period during which it is scheduled to be 
effective.
The Applicable Firm Load Commitment shall not be reduced or deferred based on:
the amount of load that actually materializes;
the amount of Firm Transmission Service actually taken to serve the Large Load 
Facilities; or
the actual operating level of the Large Load Facilities.
2. Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark
For each Measurement Period, the “Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark” shall equal 
100% of the Firm Transmission Service-related charges that would apply if Eligible Customer 
took Firm Transmission Service corresponding to the Applicable Firm Load Commitment during 
that Measurement Period.
The Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark shall be calculated using:
the Applicable Firm Load Commitment;
the Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate;
the generally applicable rate components and billing determinants used under the PJM 
Tariff and Transmission Owner’s applicable FERC-jurisdictional rate to calculate charges 
for  Firm Transmission Service; and
the portion of the Measurement Period during which each applicable load level and 
Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate applies.
If the Applicable Firm Load Commitment or Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate 
changes during a Measurement Period, the Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark shall 
equal the sum of the amounts separately calculated for each applicable portion of the 
Measurement Period.
3. Committed Revenue Contribution
For each Measurement Period, the Committed Revenue Contribution = Minimum Commitment 
Percentage × Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark
The Minimum Commitment Percentage shall be the percentage specified in Exhibit A.
Page 63

The Minimum Commitment Percentage shall be applied only to the Full Firm Transmission 
Service Benchmark and shall not be applied to the Actual Revenue Contribution.
4. Actual Revenue Contribution
For each Measurement Period, the Actual Revenue Contribution shall equal the Firm 
Transmission Service-related revenues paid or payable to PJM for remittance or allocation to 
Transmission Owner, or otherwise paid or payable to Transmission Owner, that are attributable 
to transmission service actually taken to serve the Large Load Facilities.
The Actual Revenue Contribution shall include amounts to the extent those amounts:
are attributable to Firm Transmission Service taken by Eligible Customer to serve the 
Large Load Facilities;
correspond to the same categories of rate components included in the Full Firm 
Transmission Service Benchmark; and
have not been refunded, reversed, or otherwise credited to the payer.
To the extent the applicable Firm Transmission Service methodology uses an assigned 
Network Service Peak Load contribution or another allocated billing determinant, the 
Actual Revenue Contribution shall be calculated using:
the billing determinant assigned to the Large Load Facilities for the applicable 
Measurement Period; and
the same categories of rates and rate components used to calculate the Full Firm 
Transmission Service Benchmark.
5. Actual Billing Determinant and Allocation
If Firm Transmission Service-related charges or billing determinants attributable to the Large 
Load Facilities are aggregated with charges or billing determinants attributable to other load, 
Transmission Owner shall determine the portion attributable to the Large Load Facilities using, 
in the following order of priority:
PJM billing and settlement data that separately identifies the Large Load Facilities;
metering or other load data for the Large Load Facilities, applied in accordance with the 
generally applicable billing and allocation methodology under the PJM Tariff; and
if the foregoing information is insufficient, other information supplied by Eligible 
Customer or the applicable billing or service entity that Transmission Owner reasonably 
determines is sufficient to identify and verify the portion attributable to the Large Load 
Facilities.
Eligible Customer shall provide, or cause the applicable billing or service entity to provide, 
information reasonably necessary to identify and verify the portion attributable to the Large Load 
Facilities.
6. Included Rate Components
Page 64

The same categories of Firm Transmission Service rate components shall be used to calculate the 
Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark and the Actual Revenue Contribution.  The included 
rate components shall be derived from the applicable zonal Firm Transmission Service rate.
The following amounts shall be excluded:
charges for electric energy;
charges for generation capacity;
retail electric service or distribution-service charges;
penalties or charges for unreserved transmission use;
administrative-service or ancillary-service charges, unless expressly included above;
interest, late-payment charges, taxes, and fees unrelated to the included Firm 
Transmission Service rate components; and
amounts attributable to load other than the Large Load Facilities.
7. Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate
The Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate for each Measurement Period shall be the 
applicable zonal rate then in effect under the PJM Tariff and Transmission Owner’s FERC-
jurisdictional rate for Firm Transmission Service in the applicable Transmission Zone.
If an applicable zonal Firm Transmission Service Rate changes during a Measurement Period, 
each rate shall apply to the portion of the Measurement Period during which it was in effect.
8. Shortfall Amount
For each Measurement Period, the Shortfall Amount = Committed Revenue Contribution • 
Actual Revenue Contribution
If the Actual Revenue Contribution equals or exceeds the Committed Revenue Contribution, the 
Shortfall Amount shall be zero.
9. Separate Measurement Periods
Each Measurement Period shall be calculated independently. Any amount by which the Actual 
Revenue Contribution exceeds the Committed Revenue Contribution for one Measurement 
Period shall not reduce a Shortfall Amount for another Measurement Period, be carried forward 
or backward, or entitle Large Load Customer to any payment, refund, or credit.
10. Partial Measurement Periods
For any partial Measurement Period, the Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark, Committed 
Revenue Contribution, Actual Revenue Contribution, and Shortfall Amount shall be calculated 
for the portion of the Measurement Period falling within the Term.
The Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark shall be prorated in accordance with the billing 
interval applicable to the Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate, based on the portion of the

EXHIBIT C
CREDIT SUPPORT REQUIREMENT AND SCHEDULE
1. Credit Support Requirement
The Credit Support Requirement is intended to secure Large Load Customer’s projected 
financial exposure under the CRA for the remaining Term and does not determine or limit any 
amount otherwise payable by Large Load Customer under the CRA.
At execution by the Parties, the Initial Credit Support Requirement shall be calculated using the 
Initial Load Commitment, anticipated Service Dates, estimated Applicable Firm Transmission 
Service Rate, and other information then available, and the methodology specified below. 
The Initial Credit Support Requirement shall equal the aggregate Projected Full Firm 
Transmission Service Benchmarks for the full Term of this CRA beginning on the first Service 
Date through the end of the Term.
Following the update required under Section 3.2 after execution of the Final PJM Agreement, 
Transmission Owner shall recalculate the Credit Support Requirement using the updated Firm 
Load Commitment, Service Dates, Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate, and Projected 
Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmarks for the remainder of the Term. The recalculated 
Credit Support Requirement shall replace the Initial Credit Support Requirement.
At the end of each Measurement Period, Transmission Owner shall recalculate Large Load 
Customer’s Credit Support Requirement. The recalculation shall equal the aggregate Projected 
Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmarks for the remaining Term. Transmission Owner shall 
exclude a completed Measurement Period from the Credit Support Requirement only after:
(i) Transmission Owner has finally calculated the Committed Revenue Contribution, Actual 
Revenue Contribution, and any resulting Shortfall Amount for that Measurement Period; and
(ii) Large Load Customer has paid all amounts due for that Measurement Period.
Transmission Owner shall provide Large Load Customer with notice after each recalculation, 
and the revised Credit Support Requirement shall become effective in accordance with Section 
6.5 of the CRA. These recalculations shall not constitute an amendment to this Exhibit or the 
CRA.
2. Calculation of Projected Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmarks
For each Measurement Period included in the Credit Support Requirement, the Projected Full 
Firm Transmission Service Benchmark shall equal 100% of the Firm Transmission Service-
related charges that would apply if Eligible Customer took Firm Transmission Service 
corresponding to the Initial Load Commitment or Firm Load Commitment, as applicable, 
scheduled to apply during that Measurement Period.
The Credit Support Requirement shall equal the aggregate Projected Full Firm Transmission 
Service Benchmarks for all Measurement Periods included in the applicable calculation.

The Projected Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark shall be calculated using:
the Initial Load Commitment or Firm Load Commitment, as applicable, and set forth in 
Exhibit A;
the Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate in effect or estimated to apply, as 
applicable, at the time of calculation;
any rate change accepted by FERC and scheduled to become effective during the 
applicable Measurement Period;
the rate components and billing determinants identified in Exhibit B; and
the portion of each Measurement Period during which each applicable load level and 
Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate is scheduled to apply.
3. No Reduction for Minimum Commitment Percentage or Projected Actual Revenues
The Credit Support Requirement shall be calculated using 100% of the Projected Full Firm 
Transmission Service Benchmarks and shall not be reduced by:
the Minimum Commitment Percentage; or
any projected or estimated Actual Revenue Contribution.
Actual Revenue Contributions shall be credited in determining the Shortfall Amount for a 
completed Measurement Period in accordance with Article 5 and Exhibit B.
After the calculation for a completed Measurement Period has been finalized and Large Load 
Customer has paid all amounts due for that Measurement Period, that Measurement Period shall 
be excluded from the Credit Support Requirement in accordance with Sections 1 and 4 of this 
Exhibit.
For avoidance of doubt, Actual Revenue Contributions attributable to a completed Measurement 
Period shall not reduce the Projected Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark for any future 
Measurement Period.

Early Termination Amount = (Applicable Termination Percentage × Present Value of Remaining 
Projected Committed Revenue Contributions) • Applicable Credits 
The Applicable Termination Percentage used in the calculation shall be the percentage specified 
in Section 1 of this Exhibit for the date on which the termination becomes effective.
Before execution of the Final PJM Agreement, the Early Termination Amount shall be calculated 
using the Initial Load Commitment, anticipated Service Dates, estimated Applicable Firm 
Transmission Service Rate, and other information then reflected in Exhibits A and C. After 
execution of the Final PJM Agreement, the calculation shall use the updated information 
provided pursuant to Section 3.2.
The Early Termination Amount shall not be less than zero.
3. Present Value of Remaining Projected Committed Revenue Contributions
The Present Value of Remaining Projected Committed Revenue Contributions shall be 
calculated as of the effective date of termination for the period beginning on the effective date of 
termination and ending on the date the fixed period specified in Section 4.2(i) of the CRA would 
have expired absent the termination.
Page 71

The calculation shall be based on:
the Initial Load Commitment or Firm Load Commitment, as applicable, and Service 
Dates in effect immediately before termination;
the Minimum Commitment Percentage;
the Projected Full Firm Transmission Service Benchmark determined in accordance with 
Exhibit C;
the Applicable Firm Transmission Service Rate in effect or estimated to apply, as 
applicable, on the effective date of termination; 
any rate change accepted by FERC and scheduled to become effective during the 
remaining fixed period;
the rate components and billing determinants identified in Exhibit B; and
Transmission Owner’s then-effective FERC-approved weighted average cost of capital as 
the discount rate.
No rate escalation or other projected rate change shall be included unless the rate change has 
been accepted by FERC and is scheduled to become effective during the remaining fixed period.
4. Applicable Credits
Applicable Credits shall include, without duplication:
any Actual Revenue Contribution attributable to the portion of the Measurement Period 
occurring before the effective date of termination that has been paid or is payable and has 
not otherwise been credited;
any Shortfall Amount, Credit Support proceeds, or other amount previously collected and 
applied to the same revenue exposure; and
any Early Termination Offset Amount determined under Section 9.9 of the CRA.
No amount shall be treated as an Applicable Credit unless it has been paid, received, or applied 
to the revenue exposure included in the Early Termination Amount.
5. Partial Termination Amount
Unless the permanently reduced portion of the Firm Load Commitment consists of a separately 
identifiable load tranche, the Partial Termination Amount shall equal:
Partial Termination Amount = Early Termination Amount × (Permanently Reduced MW ÷ 
applicable Initial Load Commitment or Firm Load Commitment immediately before reduction) 
The Applicable Termination Percentage shall be the percentage specified in Section 1 of this 
Exhibit for the effective date of the Partial Termination.
If the permanently reduced portion consists of one or more separately identifiable load tranches, 
the Partial Termination Amount shall be calculated using the Projected Committed Revenue 
Contributions attributable to the terminated tranche or tranches, including the applicable MW 
amount and Service Date for each terminated tranche.
Page 72

The Partial Termination Amount shall not be less than zero.
6. Treatment After the First Service Date
On and after the first Service Date, the Applicable Termination Percentage shall remain 100%.
The Present Value of Remaining Projected Committed Revenue Contributions will decline as the 
remaining portion of the fixed period decreases. Accordingly, the Applicable Termination 
Percentage will not be separately reduced based solely on the passage of time after the first 
Service Date.
7. Early Termination Offset Amount
If an Early Termination Offset Amount is quantifiable when Transmission Owner issues the 
applicable termination invoice, Transmission Owner shall include that amount as an Applicable 
Credit.
If all or part of the Early Termination Offset Amount becomes quantifiable after the termination 
invoice is issued, Transmission Owner shall reflect the amount in a subsequent reconciliation and 
promptly return any resulting excess payment to Large Load Customer in accordance with 
Articles 7 and 9 of the CRA.
Nothing in this Exhibit requires Transmission Owner to market the Point of Delivery, solicit 
replacement load, modify its transmission planning or service processes, or enter into a 
transmission-service arrangement with another Person.
8. No Duplicate Recovery
The Early Termination Amount and Partial Termination Amount are forward-looking amounts 
intended to address projected revenue exposure arising after the effective date of termination or 
Partial Termination.
Transmission Owner shall not recover the same revenue exposure through both:
a Shortfall Amount; and
an Early Termination Amount or Partial Termination Amount.
Amounts collected before termination or Partial Termination shall be credited only to the extent 
required under Article 9 and this Exhibit to prevent duplicate recovery.

11)
Determining the Border Yearly Charge
(A) Formula for Determining the Border Yearly Charge
(i)  Beginning with the calendar year 2020, the Border Yearly Charge shall be based on the following formula:
BYC = SHRR/SZPL
Where:
BYC is the Border Yearly Charge stated in dollars per kW of Reserved Capacity; 
SHRR is the sum of the Revenue Requirements for each Transmission Owner used to determine charges for Network Integration Transmission Service either (a) 
stated in Attachment H for a Transmission Owner or (b) determined pursuant to a formula rate set forth in Attachment H, both as adjusted in accordance with this 
section (11)(A). 
SZPL is the sum of each Zone’s annual peak load (in kW) plus the peak day firm reservations for Point-to-Point service at the Border of PJM (in kW) subject to the 
charges set forth in section (1) herein (prior to any applicable discount) from the most recently completed 12-month period ending October 31.
(ii) Where the Revenue Requirement of a Transmission Owner is determined pursuant to a formula rate: 
(a) the Revenue Requirement shall be increased by the amount of any revenue included in the Transmission Owner’s formula rate as credits in 
determining the Revenue Requirement for Network Integration Transmission Service from: (i) Transmission Enhancement Charges; (ii) Firm Point-to-Point 
Transmission Service charges under Schedule 7; or (iii) Network Integration Transmission Service to Non-Zone Network Load under Attachment H-A; (iv) 
Interconnection Reliability Reinforcement Charges;  or (v) Generator Reliability Reinforcement Recovery Fees that are included in the Transmission Owner’s 
formula rate as revenue credits in determining the Revenue Requirement for Network Integration Transmission Service, if such credits are identified in the 
Transmission Owner’s formula rate annual update; and

(b)  (I) the Revenue Requirement shall be reduced by the amount of any credit applied directly to Network Customers to offset the cost of Network 
Integration Transmission Service, including credits to Network Customers resulting from: (i) a Network Upgrade Funding Agreement, Tariff, Attachment O-2; (ii) a 
State Agreement Public Policy Project subject to Tariff, Schedule 12, section (b)(xii)(B);  (iii) agreements for transmission service entered into prior to a 
Transmission Owner signing the Consolidated Transmission Owners Agreement or any of its predecessor agreements or (iv) an entity executing an agreement by 
which such entity is obligated to pay for some, or all, of the Revenue Requirement of Transmission Facilities for which Network Customers would otherwise be 
responsible. (II) The Revenue Requirement for inclusion in the SHRR shall not be reduced by the amount of any credits for (i) Transmission Enhancement Charges; 
(ii) Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Service charges under this Schedule 7; or (iii) Network Integration Transmission Service to Non-Zone Network Load under 
Tariff, Attachment H-A; (iv) Interconnection Reliability Reinforcement Charges;  or (v) Generator Reliability Reinforcement Recovery Fees.
(B) The Transmission Provider shall update the Border Yearly Charge annually based on the Revenue Requirements for each Transmission Owner used to

(iii)
DFAX Analysis for Reliability Projects.  
(A)  For purposes of the assignment of cost responsibility for Reliability Projects 
under subsection (b)(i)(A)(2)(a) and subsection (b)(ii)(A) of this Schedule 12, the Transmission 
Provider, based on a computer model of the electric network and using power flow modeling 
software, shall calculate distribution factors, represented as decimal values or percentages, which 
express the portions of a transfer of energy from a defined source to a defined sink that will flow 
across a particular transmission facility or group of transmission facilities.  These distribution 
factors represent a measure of the use by the load of each Zone or Merchant Transmission 
Facility (collectively, “Responsible Zone”) of the Required Transmission Enhancement, as 
determined by a power flow analysis.  In general, a distribution factor can be represented as:
Distribution Factor = (After-shift power flow – pre-shift power flow) / Total amount of power 
shifted
Total amount of power shifted = Modeled incremental megawatt transfer to a given Load 
Deliverability Area or Merchant Transmission Facility
Pre-shift power flow = Megawatt flow over the Required Transmission Enhancement  
before the incremental megawatt transfer
After-shift power flow = Megawatt flow over the Required Transmission Enhancement 
after the incremental megawatt transfer
When calculating such distribution factors:
(1)
All distribution factors are calculated with respect to the Required 
Transmission Enhancement subject to cost allocation under subsection (b)(i)(A)(2)(a) and 
subsection (b)(ii)(A) of this Schedule 12.
(2)
The calculation of distribution factors shall be determined using 
linear matrix algebra, such that distribution factors represent the ratio of (i) a change in megawatt 
flow on a Required Transmission Enhancement to (ii) a change in megawatts transferred to 
aggregate load within a Zone or, in the case of a Merchant Transmission Facility, the point of 
withdrawal associated with Firm Transmission Withdrawal Rights over such Merchant 
Transmission Facility.

(3)
With respect to a Merchant Transmission Facility, zonal peak load 
shall mean (i) the existing Firm Transmission Withdrawal Rights of the Merchant Transmission 
Facility being evaluated, if the Merchant Transmission Facility is in service, or (ii) for a 
Merchant Transmission Facility that is not yet in service, the planned Firm Transmission 
Withdrawal Rights of the Merchant Transmission Facility being evaluated as identified in the 
Interconnection Service Agreement in effect for such Merchant Transmission Facility. 
(4)
In the DFAX analysis, when Transmission Provider models a 
transfer from generation to all load within an individual Zone, Transmission Provider shall 
model the transfer to the Zone as a whole (not on a bus-by-bus basis).  
(5)
In the DFAX analysis, Transmission Provider shall model 
generation both external and internal to individual Responsible Zones to reflect (a) the 
boundaries of Locational Deliverability Areas (“LDAs”), and (b) limitations with respect to the 
reliability objective for moving generation capacity across the transmission system.  
Transmission Provider shall adopt the Capacity Emergency Transfer Objective (“CETO”), 
associated with that LDA and calculated for the applicable planning year to be the transfer 
limitation into the LDA.  In modeling the system generation and load, Transmission Provider 
shall assume that the percentage of the zonal load in the LDA served by external (or internal) 
generation to the LDA shall equal the ratio of (i) the CETO associated within that LDA (or 
generation internal with the LDA) to (ii) the sum of (a) the internal generation within the LDA 
and (b) the CETO associated with that LDA.  For the generation dispatch used in calculating the 
distribution factor, Transmission Provider shall distribute these amounts of external/internal 
generation among all generation in the PJM Region external to/internal within the LDA, 
respectively, in proportion to their capacity.  For Responsible Zones that are located within 
LDAs that are also entirely contained in other larger LDAs, the modeling approach and 
distribution factor calculations shall be repeated for such Responsible Zones for each LDA.  The 
lowest distribution factor derived from these calculations shall be applied to the Responsible 
Zone in the calculation of the use of the Required Transmission Enhancement.  
(B) 
The DFAX analysis will be performed in accordance with the following 
steps:
(1)
Transmission Provider shall calculate a distribution factor and a 
direction of use for each Responsible Zone by modeling a transfer from all generation in the PJM 
Region to each Responsible Zone.  To establish the use by a Responsible Zone, in megawatts, of 
a Required Transmission Enhancement, the distribution factor of a Required Transmission 
Enhancement associated with the resulting transfer modeled by the Transmission Provider to 
each Responsible Zone shall be multiplied by the Responsible Zone’s peak load.
(2)
The Transmission Provider shall separately determine the relative 
use of the Required Transmission Enhancement by each Responsible Zone in each direction by 
dividing the megawatts of use by each Responsible Zone determined in section (iii)(B)(1) above

by the total use of all Responsible Zones using the Required Transmission Enhancement in the 
same direction of use.
(3) 
Transmission Provider shall determine the direction of use 
percentage of the Required Transmission Enhancement in each direction using a production cost 
analysis to determine the total use, in megawatt-hours, of the Required Transmission 
Enhancement by all Zones and Merchant Transmission Facilities in each direction over the 
course of a year.  The Transmission Provider shall calculate the percentage use in each direction 
by dividing the megawatt-hours of use in each direction by total use in megawatt-hours in both 
directions of use.
(4)
The Transmission Provider shall multiply the relative use by each 
Responsible Zone of the Required Transmission Enhancement in each direction of use 
determined in section (iii)(B)(2) above, by the applicable direction of use percentage determined 
in section (iii)(B)(3) above.

The products of the calculation performed in section (iii)(B)(4)

(xviii) Required Transmission Enhancements Designed to Address Stability Issues.
For purposes of the assignment of cost responsibility for Reliability Projects designed to address 
stability issues under subsection (b)(i)(A)(2)(a) and subsection (b)(ii)(A) of this Schedule 12, the 
Transmission Provider shall, using the same inputs and assumptions from the simulation that 
originally drove the need for the stability upgrade, perform a stability simulation that includes 
the stability upgrade under the worst fault condition. The worst fault condition shall be the fault 
condition in the simulation that produces the maximum rotor angle swing with the stability 
upgrade included.  For each load bus on the system, the difference between the highest and 
lowest voltage angle that occurs during the simulation of the worst fault condition will be 
recorded. Load buses having a voltage angle deviation less than 25 percent of the load bus with 
the largest voltage angle deviation will not be included in the cost allocation calculation. For the 
Page 103

remaining load buses, the voltage angle deviation will be multiplied by the megawatt load at the 
bus obtained from the stability simulation model, or, in the case of a Merchant Transmission 
Facility, the Firm Transmission Withdrawal Rights at the bus. The products of the voltage angle 
deviation and megawatt load at each bus will be summed for each Responsible Zone. The 
Stability Deviation cost allocation for a Responsible Zone or Merchant Transmission Facility 
will be determined by dividing the sum of the load-weighted angle deviations for the 
Responsible Zone or Merchant Transmission Facility by the sum of the load-weighted angle 
deviations for each Responsible Zone and Merchant Transmission Facility. Transmission 
Provider shall round cost responsibility assignments to the nearest one-hundredth of one percent.

SCHEDULE 22
Financial Penalty Charge for 
Unreserved Use by Eligible Load and Large Load
An Eligible Customer taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service, or Interim Network Integration Transmission Service on behalf 
of Eligible Load or Large Load shall be subject to financial penalties for its unreserved use of the 
transmission system.
The financial penalty charge for unreserved use shall include two components: (1) a base penalty 
charge, which applies to each individual hour in which the reserved transmission service limit is 
exceeded, and (2) a penalty ratchet, which applies when such exceedances occur repeatedly.
Base Penalty Charge
When an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Eligible Load or Large Load exceeds its 
reserved transmission service limit, a base penalty charge shall be assessed for any hour in which 
at least one five-minute interval occurs during which the Eligible Customer’s telemetered load at 
the Point of Delivery exceeds its reserved transmission service limit.  This five-minute interval is 
defined as an Exceedance Interval, and such an hour is defined as an Exceedance Hour.  The 
base penalty charge shall apply to each Exceedance Hour.  
For an Eligible Customer taking only Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, the 
reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service minus any curtailed MW.  
For an Eligible Customer taking only Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, 
the reserved transmission service limit shall equal the approved Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service minus any curtailed MW.  
For an Eligible Customer taking Firm Contract Demand and Non-Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Services, the reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service plus the approved Non-Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service minus any curtailed MW.  
For an Eligible Customer taking Interim Network Integration Transmission Service, the 
reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Interim Network Integration 
Transmission Service demand minus any curtailed MW.
Each five-minute interval beginning with the first minute of each hour shall constitute a 
separate interval and each hour from 0100 through 2400 shall constitute a separate hour 
for purposes of determining whether one or more exceedances have occurred.
Page 115

The base penalty charge shall be applied to each Exceedance Hour and shall be calculated as:
Hourly Exceedance MW × Equivalent Hourly Firm Contract Demand (“FCD”) rate × 
number of Exceedance Intervals within the hour
Where:
Hourly Exceedance MW = Maximum telemetered load during the hour – Reserved 
Transmission Service Limit for the hour
Equivalent Hourly FCD rate = FCD rate / 8,760 hours
Penalty Ratchet
A penalty rachet shall apply when multiple Exceedance Hours occur during a particular time 
period in order to escalate the penalty charges as the frequency of unreserved transmission use 
increases.  
If more than one Exceedance Hour occurs on the same calendar day, an additional daily 
penalty shall apply.  
If exceedances occur on multiple calendar days within the same calendar week, an 
additional weekly penalty shall apply. 
If exceedances occur in multiple calendar weeks within the same calendar month, an 
additional monthly penalty shall apply.
If exceedances occur in multiple calendar months within the same calendar year, an 
additional yearly penalty shall apply.  
The penalty ratchet shall be based on an Eligible Customer’s exceedance pattern and applies 
escalating FCD-equivalent rates as the frequency of unreserved transmission use increases.  
Depending on whether exceedances occur within the same calendar day, calendar week, calendar 
month, or calendar year, the penalty ratchet shall apply daily, weekly, monthly, or annual penalty 
charges, respectively, as follows:

Customer is responsible for 100 percent of its remaining committed revenue obligation in 
2 
the event of termination.  
3 
Q.
Why is the Termination Amount based on the minimum revenue obligation rather 
4 
than projected full transmission revenues, as used to calculate the Credit Support 
5 
Requirement? 
6 
A. 
[Hammer] The Termination Amount represents an actual payment obligation, whereas the 
7 
Credit Support Requirement represents financial security for potential exposure.  Because 
8 
the Large Load Customer’s contractual minimum revenue obligation is determined by 
9 
applying the Minimum Commitment Percentage to projected transmission revenues, it is 
10 
reasonable for the Termination Amount to be based on that committed revenue obligation 
11 
rather than 100 percent of projected revenues.  This distinction ensures that the more 
12 
conservative Credit Support Requirement provides financial assurance against potential 
13 
exposure without converting that higher level of security into a greater payment obligation 
14 
upon termination. 
15 
Thus, the two provisions serve different but complementary purposes: Credit 
16 
Support secures the Transmission Owner’s full projected exposure, while the Termination 
17 
Amount reflects the Large Load Customer’s contractual payment responsibility upon 
18 
termination.61
19 
61

Q.

1 
mitigating potential cost shifts associated with Large Loads among wholesale 
2 
transmission customers? 
3 
A. 
[Hammer] Yes. The proposed CRA provides an appropriate set of financial protections 
4 
designed to mitigate the risk that costs associated with serving a Large Load will be shifted 
5 
to other wholesale transmission customers.  It achieves this through a set of  interlocking 
6 
mechanisms. 
7 
The proposed CRA establishes a minimum revenue commitment to provide a 
8 
defined level of transmission revenue even if the Large Load does not materialize or ramp 
9 
as expected. It requires Credit Support based on 100 percent of projected Firm 
10 
Transmission Service revenues, providing a strong financial backstop for the Transmission 
11 
Owner’s potential exposure.  And, if the customer terminates or reduces its commitment, 
12 
the early and partial termination provisions require the customer to bear an appropriate 
13 
portion of its remaining committed revenue obligation.62
14 
Collectively, these provisions appropriately allocate the financial risks associated 
15 
with the Large Load Customer’s Firm Transmission Service commitment to that customer, 
16 
while calibrating the customer’s payment and Credit Support obligations to the nature and 
17 
extent of the exposure being addressed. 
18

19 
A. 
[Blazunas and Hammer] Yes.
